Three logistics solutions approved
body:
The Government today announced a first batch of three preapproved information technology onboarding solutions under the Future Innovative Logistics Acceleration Scheme.

 

Eligible third-party logistics service providers can now apply for funding support in subscribing to or using these solutions. Individual enterprises can receive funding support of up to $2million.

 

Twenty-six applications were received after providers were earlier invited to apply for their IT onboarding solutions to be included on a white list of preapproved solutions under the scheme.

 

The Hong Kong Productivity Council (HKPC), the Logistics & Supply Chain MultiTech R&D Centre and the Airport Authority assessed the applications based on their compatibility with relevant logistics data platforms, functionality, usability, security and project management planning. The three highest-scoring solutions were selected for the first batch of preapproved solutions to be included on the white list.

 

The Transport & Logistics Bureau said that digitalisation is a key priority for the logistics industry to maintain its competitiveness.

 

With the availability of preapproved solutions under the scheme, the bureau hopes that service provides will seize the opportunity to digitalise their businesses and explore the benefits offered by logistics data platforms including greater logistics transparency, more efficient supply chain management and trade financing opportunities.

 

Details of the pilot scheme and relevant application materials are available on its dedicated website. Interested service providers can call 2788 6077 or email the HKPC.

title: CE meets UGC members
body:
Chief Executive John Lee today met the University Grants Committee (UGC) to exchange views on the latest developments in Hong Kong’s higher education sector.

 

The discussion focused on several key areas, including strengthening the integration of industry, academia and research through the Northern Metropolis University Town Area development. The meeting also covered building Hong Kong into an international education hub through national and global partnerships, as well as promoting the city’s leadership role in research, teaching and learning in the digital era.

 

UGC Chairman Tim Lui briefed Mr Lee on the committee's latest strategic initiatives to reinforce Hong Kong's position as an international post-secondary education hub. These initiatives include organising high-profile summits and forums to facilitate forward-looking exchanges with global academic leaders and stakeholders.

 

Mr Lui noted that these events will explore how local higher education can align with national development priorities and Hong Kong's strategic planning objectives, thereby showcasing the city’s academic achievements and promoting the “Study in Hong Kong” brand. He added that the UGC actively supports local institutions in nurturing local talent and attracting global talent.

 

Mr Lee thanked the UGC members for their advice and their ongoing efforts to enhance the internationalisation and diversification of UGC-funded universities. Highlighting Hong Kong's widely recognised global standing, he stated that the development prospects for higher education in the city remain highly promising.

 

Mr Lee announced that the Government will soon release Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan to actively align with the National 15th Five-Year Plan. This plan will advance core strategies such as accelerating the Northern Metropolis development, growing into an international innovation and technology centre, and building a hub for high-calibre talent.

 

The Government will adopt a town area concept for the Northern Metropolis University Town, integrating education, technology, talent, industry and urban development. Mr Lee emphasised that this approach will create a high-quality university town area that drives synergy in industry, academia and research.

 

He said that through digital transformation, deepening collaboration and international partnerships, the Government will consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading education hub, strive for research excellence and nurture future-ready talent.

 

The meeting was attended by Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki, Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin, Acting Secretary for Innovation, Technology & Industry Lillian Cheong, Head of the Chief Executive's Policy Unit Stephen Wong, and Permanent Secretary for Education May Chan.

title: 3rd InnoHK research cluster launched
body:
The Innovation & Technology Commission today held a launch ceremony for the third InnoHK research cluster, SEAM@InnoHK, which focuses on four frontier technology fields: sustainable development, energy, advanced manufacturing and materials.

 

Eight research centres have been approved for admission to SEAM@InnoHK, receiving total government funding support of around $2.5 billion. Led by renowned local and overseas universities and research institutions, these centres have established collaborations with top-tier partners from the Chinese Mainland and worldwide, creating a network that includes the UK, France, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Japan.

 

Speaking at the launch ceremony, Secretary for Innovation, Technology & Industry Prof Sun Dong said that the research of the eight research centres spans next-generation semiconductors, sustainable energy, innovative materials, space manufacturing, advanced manufacturing technologies and smart energy management. He noted that the initiative echoes the call to drive high-end manufacturing, accelerate growth of strategic emerging industries, and deepen the green transition under the National 15th Five-Year Plan.

 

Prof Sun added that by integrating advanced technologies into local industries, the third research cluster demonstrates the Government's unwavering commitment to promoting real-world applications of research outcomes to accelerate Hong Kong's development into an international innovation and technology (I&T) centre.

 

The participating institutions include many of the world's top 100 universities and research and development institutes in frontier technology fields. This demonstrates Hong Kong's unique advantage as a “super connector” to seamlessly bridge top-tier international academic resources with local industrial needs.

 

Currently, the eight research centres are preparing to set up their laboratories and will come into operation progressively to inject new momentum into Hong Kong's I&T ecosystem. As a flagship international I&T initiative of the Government, InnoHK aims to bring together world-class institutions and local universities to establish premier research centres in the city.

title: Going global seminar held
body:
The Task Force on Supporting Mainland Enterprises in Going Global today held a seminar to promote Hong Kong's unique advantages in going global and the opportunities offered by the Northern Metropolis (NM).

 

More than 120 representatives of central and other state-owned enterprises preparing to attend the 11th Belt & Road Summit joined the "Set Sail from Hong Kong, Harness the Power of the Northern Metropolis – Mainland Enterprises Going Global Seminar".

 

Addressing the seminar, Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Algernon Yau said that Hong Kong, with its international business environment, world-class professional services, and top-tier talent, is the best home port for enterprises setting sail overseas.

 

Under his leadership, the task force helps enterprises go global in an orderly manner through a three-step approach of "bringing in", making preparations in Hong Kong for going global, and "reaching out".

 

He added that the NM offers enormous development potential and ample land for industrial use, which are conducive to enterprises establishing and growing their operations in Hong Kong and venturing into overseas markets with the support of Hong Kong's world-class professional services.

 

The seminar featured two thematic discussions. The first explored the industrial layout of the NM and how the opportunities arising from its modern logistics ecosystem can help internationalise the businesses of Mainland enterprises.

 

The second examined how Mainland enterprises can leverage Hong Kong's advantages to respond to the new dynamics of global commodity markets and the strains on overseas supply chains, as well as how to optimise overseas trade, commodity hedging and risk management.

title: Sci-Tech cluster maintains global lead
body:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today welcomed the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) ranking of the Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou cluster as first globally again in its Global Innovation Index 2026 top 100 innovation clusters.

 

The Government stated that the ranking reaffirmed the outstanding innovative capacity and the vibrant innovation and technology (I&T) financing ecosystem of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

 

WIPO evaluates world-class innovation hubs using three key metrics: international patent-filings via the Patent Cooperation Treaty, scientific publications and venture capital deals. For this year's index, the Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou cluster recorded 2,259 Patent Cooperation Treaty applications, 4,060 scientific articles and 138 venture capital deals per 1 million inhabitants over the past five years.

 

Expediting I&T development remains a top policy priority for the current-term Government, and those efforts have started to bear fruit. The number of start-ups rose from over 1,500 in 2015 to more than 5,200 in 2025, while the city’s two I&T flagships – Hong Kong Science Park and Cyberport – have collectively nurtured around 20 unicorn enterprises.

 

Infrastructure expansion has further boosted regional integration. The Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science & Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone (the Loop Hong Kong Park) officially opened in December last year, with over 100 technology enterprises and institutions already signing leases.

 

By leveraging the advantages of the alliance between Hong Kong and Shenzhen, the Loop Hong Kong Park will serve as an international platform for basic scientific research, commercialisation and pilot production, driving high-quality development.

 

Additionally, the San Tin Technopole Company Limited was established in June this year to drive the development of 210 hectares of I&T land. This hub will form a vital node connecting upstream, midstream and downstream industries alongside the Loop Hong Kong Park.

 

Hong Kong also maintains a robust private equity market with assets under management close to US$250 billion, ranking second in Asia after the Chinese Mainland. 

 

Looking ahead, the Government added that Hong Kong will proactively align with the National 15th Five-Year Plan to strengthen the city’s strategic position as an international I&T centre. It emphasised that Hong Kong will further deepen collaboration with the Greater Bay Area sister cities, contributing to the country's efforts in building a modern industrial system and achieving high-level scientific and technological self-reliance and strength.
